protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for DR-004 under adopted D-054 / D-057; new cycle after CONTESTED D-059
summary: Both the subject and the prompt held frozen start to end, and both were read-only at both ends. That is the first dispatch in this family where the freeze covered the instruction as well as the artifact, which is exactly the gap that put D-059 into CONTESTED. The entry is a genuine new cycle rather than a disguised fourth turn: I diffed it against the CONTESTED D-059 subject and it carries a new ID, a new provenance paragraph pinning the CONTESTED commit, a re-measured COORD, a new overturn commit, and an explicit 'Does not adopt CONTESTED D-059'. The predecessor finding it names is addressed at the bytes — nothing in this file self-identifies as turn 2. Every pin verifies: six digests, five commits, the Route A remainder an exact three-item match against the disposition's own field, and D-054, D-057 and D-048 each still ADOPTED while D-059 is CONTESTED and not adopted.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 414fbc921b10bd7ecea1141891678d6a1dec95cd5bf4895057448c8c94b3ff3c, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, permissions -r--r--r-- at both ends.

Prompt digest at start and end: 28bc6bdd619e49a619171b547c5b7c5ea9ed812c8b34e26969a99cfd570d5c58, also read-only at both ends. The dispatch made prompt motion an OBJECT condition alongside subject motion, and neither occurred. This is the direct repair of the gap I recorded as NOTE-C2-D059-T3-02, where the subject was locked and the prompt was not.

The attack 'treats this as D-059 turn 4' fails, tested by diff rather than by reading the header. Against the CONTESTED D-059 turn-3 subject at 28719de6, this file removes fourteen lines and adds eleven: the title becomes D-064, the protocol line becomes 'turn 1 of 3. Not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-059', the D-059 turn-history paragraph is replaced by a provenance paragraph pinning the CONTESTED commit, COORD is re-measured, the D-059 CONTESTED commit is added as a measured input, clause 5 gains 'Does not adopt CONTESTED D-059', and the overturn commit moves from C-D059 to C-D064.

The new cycle is lawful on the register's own terms. Adopted D-059 records 'CONTESTED after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted. No forced consensus. Parked' and states 'A later new cycle (not turn 4 of this cycle) may retry.' D-000 clause 2 is the authority for that parking, and this is the retry it contemplates.

The predecessor finding the entry names is addressed at the bytes. It cites ADV-D059-T3-02, that the final D-059 subject self-identified as turn 2, and says 'This file is turn 1 of a new cycle.' I checked: the title is '# D-064 — Owner-record the DR-004 preview Route B disposition' with no turn suffix, and the protocol line reads 'turn 1 of 3'. Nothing in the file identifies as turn 2.

All six cited digests match live bytes: COORD e53567c0…, file 08 6547e6ac…, the D-054 user amendment, the DR-004 v2 disposition, and both v2 verdicts. The COORD pin is the current post-CONTESTED value rather than a carried-forward one.

All five cited commits resolve at full hash to the expected decisions: 29670ed… D-054, 33597e8… D-057, aa75926… D-047/D-048, 88764fa… D-049/D-050, and 624e2e3… 'D-059: CONTESTED after three turns — DR-004 owner-record'.

The register standing is as the entry describes: D-054, D-057, D-048 and D-058 are ADOPTED and not CONTESTED; D-059 is CONTESTED and not ADOPTED. So the live-adoption precondition D-057 imposes holds, and the entry does not lean on the parked decision.

The attack 'missing D-054 / D-057 / D-048 pins' fails: the Authority and dependency pins section carries the dependency declaration, the D-054 path with sha256 and commit, the D-057 commit, the D-048 Route B commit, and the D-050 coordinator-recording commit.

The attack 'missing verdict paths' fails: both verdicts appear as full paths with sha256s in the pins section and again in the measured-inputs table with 'ACCEPT 0/0'. That is the form I asked for across three earlier drafts and it is now settled.

The attack 'incomplete Route A remainder' fails, tested by string equality against the disposition's own whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA: three items each, exact match, same order, including the cross-row 'DR-002 AC-4 still names this packet' so the packet obligation DR-002 depends on is not detached.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED' and 'condition 5 / file 08' fail: the header refuses SATISFIED, file-08 edits and docs/v2/implementation; clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-004 SATISFIED. The Route A remainder above stays owed. section31 v4 stays the binding instrument, not the packet. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization'; clause 4 refuses to edit file 08; file 08 measures unchanged and git reports zero modified tracked files.

Examined and declined: the entry names ADV-D059-T3-02 but not ADV-D059-T3-01, the other Codex turn-3 finding. T3-01 was that the prompt was rewritten during review — a process failure whose remedy is in the dispatch rather than in any entry's content, and it is demonstrably applied here, since both files are locked and both held. There was no content change for the entry to record.

Examined and declined: the diff drops the D-059 cycle's own pins — its turn-1 subject digest, my turn-1 verdict at 4b6418d2, the Codex turn-1 verdict at d3d22920, and the superseded COORD. Those belong to the parked cycle, and the chain remains traceable in one hop: this entry pins the CONTESTED commit 624e2e3, and that register entry pins both turn-3 verdicts including Codex's at 99fecafa. I accepted the same one-hop predecessor pattern on D-057 turn 3 and on section31 v4.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: D-059 went CONTESTED on the two findings I had recorded as notes rather than as findings. Codex's turn-3 verdict raised ADV-D059-T3-01 as MUST-FIX, that the prompt was rewritten during review, and ADV-D059-T3-02 as SHOULD-FIX, that the subject still self-identified as turn 2. I saw both and graded both NOTE.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyIGradedThemLower: For the prompt motion I reasoned that the dispatch's stated OBJECT condition named the subject only, and the subject had held. For the turn-2 self-identification I reasoned that changing the header would have changed the digest and defeated the very freeze that had just been fixed.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyTheOtherCallWasBetter: Both reasons were about what the dispatch literally asked rather than about whether the record would be sound. A prompt that moves under a reviewer breaks reproducibility just as a moving subject does, and the fix — locking both — is cheap and was available. Codex's severity produced exactly that fix: this dispatch locks the prompt as well as the subject, and both held. My grading would have adopted an entry with the process defect still live.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: When a freeze is the control being tested, I grade the freeze as a whole rather than only the artifact the instruction happens to name. I applied that here by measuring the prompt three times and recording its permissions alongside the subject's, and I would now treat prompt motion as a finding rather than a note.
reviewerSelfCorrection.onTheRecordFairly: The register's own account is accurate: 'Decision merits passed on both sides. Process freeze failed.' Neither of us was wrong about the merits, and D-000 clause 2 recorded the disagreement rather than forcing agreement, which is the protocol working.

whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero findings. The two process defects that put D-059 into CONTESTED are both fixed here, and one of them was fixed because the other reviewer graded harder than I did — I recorded prompt motion as a note where Codex made it a MUST-FIX, and the result is a dispatch that locks both files, both of which held. I have recorded that as a self-correction rather than leaving it implicit. On the merits I re-derived rather than carried forward: six digests, five commits, the register standing of five decisions, and a string-equality check of the Route A remainder. The new-cycle claim I tested by diffing against the CONTESTED subject rather than trusting the header, and it is a real new cycle, not a fourth turn wearing a new number.
